newsitem.title: CAMEROON: U.N. team in Cameroon for second Bakassi visit.
newsitem.headline: U.N. team in Cameroon for second Bakassi visit.

text.p: A United Nations team looking into the rival claims of Nigeria and Cameroon to the Bakassi peninsula was in Cameroon on Wednesday for a second visit to the disputed oil-rich area, officials said.
The team, which visited the peninsula from the Nigerian side on September 21, was due to visit the Cameroonian side on Wednesday, they added.
It was then due to leave for Togo and talks with President Gnassingbe Eyadema, who has been mediating in the dispute.
The two African nations have clashed sporadically on the Bakassi peninsula with heavy loss of lives on both sides.
Both sides have troops entrenched in the impoverished islands whose inhabitants are mainly fishermen and speak Efik, the language of southeastern Nigeria.
Cameroon took its case to the World Court in 1994 but the court's ruling in March forbidding further fighting did not prevent clashes a month later.

Cameroon on Friday denied that its troops had attacked Nigerian positions in Bakassi during the visit by the U.N. mission as alleged by Nigerian Foreign Minister Tom Ikimi on Thursday when he received the four-member team.

"One can say with near certainty that this (charge) is designed to compromise the work of the mission as well as the planned visit to the peninsula," Cameroonian Foreign Minister Ferdinand Oyono said in a statement.
